title.narrative: Ecosystem restoration for enhanced biodiversity, productive landscapes and sustainable livelihoods in Sao Tome e Principe

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project aims to strengthen FLR actions within natural forested and grassland ecosystems, ensuring continued and sustainable provision of a wide range of environmental benefits (such as soil erosion and landslides prevention, windbreaks, shade, soil and water conservation), biological benefits (including biodiversity niches, nutrient cycling systems, and medicinal resources), social-cultural benefits (preserving local knowledge, cultural and dietary habits, land tenure systems, and local customs), and economic benefits (increased income, asset ownership, welfare services, food and feed provision, and timber and fuel-wood resources) to households and communities living within and around these areas. Furthermore, the development of short and inclusive value chains based on Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) will stimulate locally based private sector and commercial ventures (e.g., ecotourism, food chains), contributing to the local and national economy.Enhancing community capacity to undertake FLR actions through improved planning, decision-making, financial investments, training, monitoring and evaluation directly enhances policy coherence and strengthens local institution capacities through inclusive, affordable, and innovative financing mechanisms (LDCF Priority 1).The STP Child project focuses on youth and women in community-based micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), small-scale self-employed informal occupations, and farmer cooperatives. It provides opportunities for decent work that deliver fair income, social protection, prospects for personal development, and social integration, ensuring equal opportunities and treatment for all women and men. Additionally, it creates an enabling environment for local and national private sector engagement to promote innovative and inclusive rural value chains and rural investments (LDCF Priority 2).Finally, the holistic and inclusive multi-sectoral partnerships of the STP Child project at community, landscape, and national levels align with a whole-of-society approach (LDCF Priority 3). This approach enhances information and knowledge symmetry, social equity, ownership, mainstreaming, and institutionalization of adaptation solutions in the country.

To strengthen national efforts towards zero-deforestation and environmentally-sound, socially equitable and economically beneficial NTFP/wood production system and value chains with an expected positive impact on poverty reduction and climate-resilient livelihoods.
